extracted.intended_audience: comedy festival attendees, tourists, and industry professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the 2026 Just For Laughs Montréal festival programming, listing show types, headliners, venues, and industry events; useful for attendees, performers, and industry participants planning or evaluating festival participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outdoor shows — free at Place des Festivals
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2026 Just For Laughs Montréal Festival presents free outdoor shows at Place des Festivals in the heart of the Quartier des Spectacles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outdoor programming is accessible (free) and staged in the central festival district; example headliner: “Weird Al” Yankovic bringing his Bigger & Weirder Tour to Place des Festivals on July 25 at 9 p.m.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gala shows — curated mix of global stars and breakout voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Just For Laughs gala shows, hosted by top comedic talent from around the world and taped live at Théâtre Maisonneuve at Place des Arts, feature a curated mix of global stars and breakout voices from across the comedy spectrum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gala curation balances big names and emerging talent; examples and dates are given (e.g., Mike Birbiglia gala July 24 6:30 p.m., Atsuko Okatsuka July 24 9:30 p.m., Gerry Dee July 25 6:30 p.m., Gabriel 'Fluffy' Iglesias July 25 9:30 p.m.). Galas are produced/taped events intended to showcase headline-level performers alongside new voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roast Battle format — head-to-head insult battles, no-punchline limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Roast Battle Canada films live in Montréal and features Canada’s boldest comics going head-to-head in savage insult battles where no punchline is off-limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format expectation: aggressive, boundary-pushing insult comedy judged in a competitive head-to-head structure. Dates are listed as TBA; producers and performers should expect high-intensity, provocative material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concert/solo headliner shows — major comedians in prestigious venues
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of the world’s hottest comics headline solo shows at JFL in many of the city’s most prestigious venues (e.g., Salle Wilfrid-Pelletier, Olympia, Le National, MTelus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concert shows are single-performer, ticketed events sized for large venues and often feature added performances based on demand (example: Jerry Seinfeld two shows at Salle Wilfrid-Pelletier; Smosh Reads Reddit Stories added a second show after selling out). Dates and times are specified per act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety programming — diverse show formats and niche concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Festival includes a range of variety shows and themed events (e.g., Top 10 Comic To Watch, UpDating live dating/comedy, podcast-based shows, drag-based shows like Sibling Rivalry Live).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variety programming showcases different comedic forms and formats—podcasts, live dating/comedy hybrids, drag performance, radio personalities—targeting different audiences and atmospheres (examples: Girls Gotta Eat, Tracy and Martina Live!, Ron Funches, Jacqueline Novak).

rubrics_metrics.name: Club Series — thematic showcases (e.g., Brit(ish))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Club Series (example: Brit(ish)) celebrates a specific comedic style or regional tradition—here, the sharp wit and dry humour of comics from Britain (and sometimes Ireland or Commonwealth friends).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Club Series are hosted in club-sized venues (example: Gesù), run multiple nights, and focus on a coherent theme or national/regional voice; often hosted by a known comic (Mark Watson for Brit(ish)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Culture Show — boundary-breaking, stereotype-challenging programming
rubrics_metrics.description: The Culture Show continues JFL’s tradition of breaking stereotypes and boundaries, hosted by Dave Merheje with rotating guests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming intent is explicitly to challenge norms and present culturally varied comedic voices; scheduled at Club Soda with specified dates/times.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Nasty Show — intentionally filthiest and most shocking content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nasty Show is described as living up to its name and promises to be the filthiest and most shocking show at the Festival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect explicit, boundary-pushing adult material; hosted by Comedian CP with named guests, scheduled in club venues with late-evening timeslots (example: Club Soda at 9:30 p.m.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Midnight Surprise Show — unpredictable lineups and new material testing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Midnight Surprise Show is one of JFL’s most unpredictable events, with surprise lineups of top-tier comedians, many of whom may perform impromptu sets or test new material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late-night format (Studio TD at 11:59 p.m. nightly) encourages spontaneity and experimentation; past surprise guests have included Kevin Hart, Dave Chappelle, Tiffany Haddish, Amy Schumer and Judd Apatow. Producers can use this slot for testing and special drop-ins.

rubrics_metrics.name: OFF-JFL — edgy, discovery-focused programming in intimate venues
rubrics_metrics.description: OFF Just For Laughs (OFF-JFL) is the festival’s edgy sibling where comedy fans can discover their favourite new artists; shows are presented in intimate venues like Salle Claude-Léveillée, Café Cléopâtre and Théâtre Sainte-Catherine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFF-JFL emphasizes discovery and edgier or emerging talent with series such as Best of the Fest, The Montreal Show, The Queer Show (spotlighting Montréal LGBTQ+ comics), and Double Threats. Venue scale is smaller and atmosphere more experimental/intimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry programming (ComedyPRO) — professional networking, panels and screenings
rubrics_metrics.description: Daytime industry networking ComedyPRO sessions for professionals and creatives (July 22 to 25), plus fireside chats, keynotes, fan events, and screenings of Just For Laughs Shorts and Pilots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry track provides professional development, networking, content screenings and panels—useful for comedians, agents, producers and industry creatives seeking development, deals, or exposure. Additional programming details and dates to be announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and breadth of artists — international, LGBTQ+, drag, multilingual representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Programming highlights a wide range of artists and traditions (global stars and breakout voices, drag superstars, Montréal LGBTQ+ comics, international acts such as Hungarian‑American or Irish comics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Festival curation intentionally mixes nationalities, identities and performance styles across gala, concert, club, OFF and variety programming to appeal to broad audiences and spotlight underrepresented voices (examples: Monét X Change & Bob The Drag Queen, The Queer Show, Zoltan Kaszas, David Nihill).
